title: Peak isometric trunk extension moment at L5/S1 (upright standing, triaxial dynamometer), males
condition: static maximal trunk extension, upright standing, pelvis and knees fixed

quantity.name: peak extension moment (MVC)
quantity.definition: peak L5/S1 extension moment during a 5 s static extension MVC (reported with negative sign = extension)

source.authors: Lariviere C, Gagnon D, Gravel D, Arsenault AB, Dumas JP, Goyette M, Loisel P
source.sample: 14 healthy males; healthy males, no back problem in preceding 6 months, in vivo

protocol.summary: Static triaxial dynamometer: subject stands erect, knees held in extension (pad), feet stabilised by wooden blocks, pelvis stabilised by a sacral pad and two pads over the ASIS; force platform (AMTI MC6-6-1000) at shoulder level contacted by an upper-back pad; trunk assumed vertical; moments computed at the L5/S1 joint centre (located from ASIS/PSIS: 50% of ASIS-PSIS distance from PSIS, 15 mm above). One 5-s extension MVC, then three 7-s ramp contractions 0-100% MVC with real-time visual feedback of Mext.
how_to_simulate: Upright standing, pelvis fixed, trunk vertical, arms free/not used.
Apply a posterior contact force at shoulder level (upper back pad) producing a pure extension moment about L5/S1.
Compare the model's maximal extension moment at L5/S1 (or the maximal muscle stress needed to equilibrate 250.7 Nm) with data.
protocol.notes: Single primary direction (extension) only. Moment sign as printed: -250.7 Nm (extension negative in this paper's convention).

extraction.check_notes: Re-read Results: 'peak extension moment at L5/S1 reached -250.7 Nm (SD: 51.3 Nm)'.
